891.explanation: Sheikh Farid, whose verses are in the Guru Granth Sahib, warns against looking down on the dust underfoot, since in the end it covers everyone; traditional commentary reads the dust as the humble saint.
891.tie_back: The Kural's first safeguard is never to belittle those who have real strength, and Farid likewise warns that what seems low and easy to despise is greater than it looks.
891.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1378, Salok Sheikh Fareed (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
891._accuracy_note: Next-best: shares the warning against belittling, but Farid's point is humility and mortality rather than prudence toward the powerful; only the opening clause is quoted because the published translation of the rest has a typographical error.

892.quote_or_event: “One who slanders the Saints, O Nanak! Shall be reincarnated over and over again.”
892.explanation: The shalok opening the thirteenth ashtapadi of Sukhmani Sahib says that contempt for the holy brings suffering that keeps returning, birth after birth.
892.tie_back: The Kural says disregard for the great brings lasting trouble that will not go away, and Guru Arjan likewise describes a penalty that keeps coming back.
892.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 279, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa, as given on srigranth.org)
892._accuracy_note: Strong on lasting affliction for slighting the great; Gurbani's 'Saints' are the God-conscious, not the worldly powerful, and the consequence works through divine order rather than their revenge.

893.quote_or_event: “He himself must eat what he has planted.”
893.explanation: In the same passage on slandering the Saint, Guru Arjan says the slanderer reaps exactly the harvest he has sown.
893.tie_back: The Kural ironically says that whoever wants ruin need only offend the able, and Gurbani agrees that such a person brings ruin on himself.
893.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 280, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
893._accuracy_note: Reasonable fit on self-inflicted ruin; the Kural's irony and its point about those able to destroy at will are not present.

894.quote_or_event: “Slandering the Saints, one's life is cut short.”
894.explanation: Guru Arjan opens his catalogue of the slanderer's fate with the shortening of life itself.
894.tie_back: The Kural says the weak who harm the strong are beckoning Death with their own hand, and Gurbani likewise links offending the holy with an early end.
894.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 279, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
894._accuracy_note: Strong fit on offending the great as inviting death; the Kural's great ones include the powerful, while Gurbani speaks only of holy people.

895.quote_or_event: “The slanderer of the Saint has no place of rest.”
895.explanation: Guru Arjan says that one who sets himself against the holy finds no refuge anywhere.
895.tie_back: The Kural says those who incur a mighty king's anger will not survive wherever they flee, and Gurbani describes the same homelessness for the enemy of the Saint.
895.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 280, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
895._accuracy_note: Good on finding no refuge, but the Kural's subject is a king's wrath, and Sikh teaching does not counsel fear of earthly rulers; the parallel holds only for the holy.

896.quote_or_event: “Slandering the Saints, one shall not escape the Messenger of Death.”
896.explanation: Guru Arjan says there is no escape for one who wrongs the holy.
896.tie_back: The Kural says one burnt by fire may survive but those who offend the great will not escape, and Gurbani uses the same language of no escape.
896.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 279, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
896._accuracy_note: Strong on the certainty of no escape; the fire comparison is absent, and the same passage adds that the slanderer may still be saved if the Saint is merciful.

897.quote_or_event: “The slanderer of the Saint becomes miserable and poor.”
897.explanation: Guru Arjan says that wronging the holy strips away both happiness and wealth.
897.tie_back: The Kural asks what use a splendid life and great wealth are once the truly worthy are angered, and Gurbani says such a person is left miserable and poor.
897.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 280, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
897._accuracy_note: Strong fit on the loss of wealth and happiness; Gurbani attributes it to the slanderer's own wrong, not to the Saint's anger.

898.quote_or_event: “The slanderer of the Saint has no heritage at all.”
898.explanation: Guru Arjan says the slanderer is left with no roots and no lasting line.
898.tie_back: The Kural says that slighting the mountain-like great uproots even those who seemed permanent, together with their families, and Gurbani likewise speaks of a life left with no roots.
898.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 280, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
898._accuracy_note: Good fit on losing roots and lineage; the mountain image and the stress on people who seemed firmly established are absent.

899.quote_or_event: “The slanderer of the Saint breaks down mid-way.”
899.explanation: Guru Arjan says the slanderer is broken in mid-course, and elsewhere in the same passage that he has no kingdom.
899.tie_back: The Kural says that when those of lofty principle flare up, even a king is broken midway and loses his kingdom, and Gurbani uses the same image of breaking midway.
899.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 280, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
899._accuracy_note: Strong, close fit (the Kural's idai murindhu, 'broken midway', is mirrored almost exactly); Gurbani does not single out kings or make the Saint's anger the cause.

900.quote_or_event: “The slanderer of the Saint cannot be saved by anyone else.”
900.explanation: Guru Arjan says no outside protector can rescue one who sets himself against the holy, though the same verse adds that the Saint himself may forgive.
900.tie_back: The Kural says even those with boundless support and powerful allies will not survive if the truly great are angered, and Gurbani likewise says no other protector can save them.
900.source: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 280, Raag Gauree (Sukhmani), Guru Arjan (tr. Sant Singh Khalsa)
900._accuracy_note: Strong fit on allies being useless; Gurbani adds a hope of forgiveness that the Kural does not offer.
